# Contributing to Spell UI

Source: https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to Spell UI

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Spell UI! We appreciate your support and look forward to your contributions. This guide will help you understand the directory structure and provide detailed instructions on how to add a new component to Spell UI.

**You only need to change 4 files to add a new component.**

Once done, open a pull request from your forked repo to the main repo [here](https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui/compare).

## Getting Started

### Fork and Clone the Repository

1. **Fork this repository**
   Click [here](https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui/fork) to fork the repository.

2. **Clone your forked repository to your local machine**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<YOUR_USERNAME>/spell-ui.git
   ```

3. **Navigate to the project directory**

   ```bash
   cd spell-ui
   ```

4. **Create a new branch for your changes**

   ```bash
   git checkout -b my-new-component
   ```

5. **Install dependencies**

   ```bash
   pnpm i
   ```

6. **Run the project**

   ```bash
   pnpm dev
   ```

Open http://localhost:3000 to view the docs.

## Adding a New Component

To add a new component to Spell UI, you need to modify 4 files. The sidebar and doc schema are automatically generated from the registry.

### 1. Create Component

Create the main component in `registry/spell-ui/example-component.tsx`

```typescript
import React from "react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

export default function ExampleComponent({
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>) {
  return (
    <div className={cn("", className)} {...props}>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### 2. Update Registry

Add your component to `registry.json` in the `items` array:

```json
{
  "name": "example-component",
  "type": "registry:component",
  "title": "Example Component",
  "description": "A versatile component for displaying various types of content.",
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "registry/spell-ui/example-component.tsx",
      "type": "registry:component"
    }
  ],
  "dependencies": [],
  "registryDependencies": [],
  "category": "display"
}
```

Add `dependencies` (e.g. `["motion"]`) and `registryDependencies` as needed for your component.

### 3. Create Docs Directory and Demo

Create `docs/example-component/demo.tsx`:

```typescript
import ExampleComponent from "@/registry/spell-ui/example-component";

export function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="flex justify-center">
      <ExampleComponent>Your content here</ExampleComponent>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### 4. Create Documentation

Create `docs/example-component/doc.mdx`:

```mdx
import { Demo } from "./demo";

<DemoCanvas>
  <DemoPreview>
    <Demo />
  </DemoPreview>
  <DemoCode>
    ```tsx file=./demo.tsx
    ```

## Installation

<InstallationTabs item="example-component">
```tsx file=../../registry/spell-ui/example-component.tsx
```

## Usage

```tsx
import ExampleComponent from "@/components/example-component";
```

```tsx
<ExampleComponent>Your content here</ExampleComponent>
```

## Props

```tsx
<PropsTable
  data={[
    {
      name: "children",
      type: "React.ReactNode",
      nameDetails: "The content of the component"
    },
    {
      name: "className",
      type: "string",
      nameDetails: "Additional CSS classes"
    }
  ]}
/>
```

### 5. Build Registry

```bash
pnpm registry:build
```

This generates `public/r/example-component.json` for the CLI installation.

### Adding Multiple Examples

To add variant demos (e.g. sizes, colors), create additional demo files:

- `docs/example-component/demo-sizes.tsx`
- `docs/example-component/demo-colors.tsx`

Then add them to your doc.mdx:

```mdx
import { Demo } from "./demo";
import { Demo as DemoSizes } from "./demo-sizes";

<DemoCanvas>
  ...
</DemoCanvas>

### Size

<DemoCanvas>
  <DemoPreview>
    <DemoSizes />
  </DemoPreview>
  <DemoCode>
    ```tsx file=./demo-sizes.tsx
    ```
```

## Component Guidelines

- Use TypeScript
- Follow existing patterns in `registry/spell-ui/`
- Use Tailwind CSS for styling
- Prefer `motion` (Framer Motion) for animations
- Use `cn()` from `@/lib/utils` for class merging

## Ask for Help

For any help or questions, please open a new [GitHub issue](https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui/issues).

```
```tsx

<AnimatedCheckbox title="Already done" defaultChecked />
```

      name: "title",
      default: '"Implement Checkbox"',
      nameDetails: "The label text for the checkbox"
      name: "defaultChecked",
      type: "boolean",
      default: "false",
      nameDetails: "Initial checked state"
      name: "onCheckedChange",
      type: "(checked: boolean) => void",
      nameDetails: "Callback when checked state changes"
      nameDetails: "Additional CSS classes"

  <DemoPreview className="p-0">

    ```

## Installation

<InstallationTabs item="animated-gradient">
```tsx file=../../registry/spell-ui/animated-gradient.tsx
```

## Examples

### Presets

  <DemoPreview className="p-0">
    <DemoPresets />
    ```tsx file=./demo-presets.tsx
    ```

## Usage

```tsx
import AnimatedGradient from "@/components/animated-gradient";
```

```tsx
<div className="relative h-[300px] w-full">
  <AnimatedGradient config={{ preset: "Prism" }} />
  <div className="relative z-10">Your content here</div>
</div>
```

### Custom Configuration

```tsx
<AnimatedGradient
  config={{
    preset: "custom",
    color1: "#1a1a2e",
    color2: "#16213e",
    color3: "#0f3460",
    rotation: 45,
    speed: 25,
    swirl: 60,
  }}
/>
```

## Props

      name: "config",
      type: '{ preset: PresetName } | { preset: "custom"; color1: string; color2: string; color3: string; ... }',
      default: '{ preset: "Prism" }',
      nameDetails: "Gradient configuration - use a preset or custom settings"
      name: "noise",
      type: "{ opacity: number; scale?: number }",
      nameDetails: "Optional noise overlay configuration"
      name: "radius",
      default: '"0px"',
      nameDetails: "Border radius of the container"
      nameDetails: "Additional CSS classes"
      name: "style",
      type: "CSSProperties",
      nameDetails: "Additional inline styles"

### Custom Config Options

When using `preset: "custom"`, these options are available:

      name: "color1",
      default: "required",
      nameDetails: "First gradient color"
      name: "color2",
      default: "required",
      nameDetails: "Second gradient color"
      name: "color3",
      default: "required",
      nameDetails: "Third gradient color"
      name: "rotation",
      type: "number",
      default: "0",
      nameDetails: "Rotation angle (-360 to 360)"
      name: "proportion",
      type: "number",
      default: "35",
      nameDetails: "Color proportion (0-100)"
      name: "scale",
      type: "number",
      default: "1",
      nameDetails: "Scale of the pattern"
      name: "speed",
      type: "number",
      default: "25",
      nameDetails: "Animation speed (0-100)"
      name: "distortion",
      type: "number",
      default: "12",
      nameDetails: "Noise distortion (0-100)"
      name: "swirl",
      type: "number",
      default: "80",
      nameDetails: "Swirl intensity (0-100)"
      name: "swirlIterations",
      type: "number",
      default: "10",
      nameDetails: "Number of swirl layers (0-20)"
      name: "softness",
      type: "number",
      default: "100",
      nameDetails: "Edge softness (0-100)"
      name: "offset",
      type: "number",
      default: "0",
      nameDetails: "Time offset (-1000 to 1000)"
      name: "shape",
      type: '"Checks" | "Stripes" | "Edge"',
      default: '"Checks"',
      nameDetails: "Base pattern shape"
      name: "shapeSize",
      type: "number",
      default: "10",
      nameDetails: "Size of the pattern (0-100)"

  <DemoPreview className="p-6 md:p-10">

    ```tsx file=./demo-static.tsx
    ```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Chart } from "@/components/chart";
```
```tsx
const data = [12, 18, 15, 24, 22, 30, 28, 35, 42, 38, 48, 56];

<Chart data={data} />
```

The chart auto-scales the Y axis to the data range. Hover snaps to the nearest data point.

## Props

      name: "data",
      type: "number[]",
      nameDetails: "Numeric values to plot"
      name: "labels",
      type: "string[]",
      nameDetails: "Optional label for each data point"
      name: "name",
      nameDetails: "Series name shown in the tooltip"
      name: "color",
      default: "\"#0090FD\"",
      nameDetails: "Line and dot color as a hex string"
      name: "width",
      type: "number",
      default: "640",
      nameDetails: "Maximum chart width in pixels"
      name: "formatValue",
      type: "(value: number, index: number) => React.ReactNode",
      default: "v => v.toLocaleString()",
      nameDetails: "Format the tooltip value"
      name: "defaultIndex",
      type: "number",
      default: "data.length - 1",
      nameDetails: "Index of the active point on initial render"
      name: "showXAxis",
      type: "boolean",
      default: "true",
      nameDetails: "Show tick labels along the bottom"
      name: "tickCount",
      type: "number",
      default: "6",
      nameDetails: "Target number of ticks on the X axis"
      name: "reveal",
      type: "boolean",
      default: "false",
      nameDetails: "Gray the line until the cursor passes over it"
      name: "showFill",
      type: "boolean",
      default: "true",
      nameDetails: "Show the gradient fill under the line"
      name: "showDot",
      type: "boolean",
      default: "true",
      nameDetails: "Show the colored dot at the active point"
      name: "animated",
      type: "boolean",
      default: "true",
      nameDetails: "Animate the cursor, dot, and tooltip on hover"
      nameDetails: "Additional CSS classes"

# doc.mdx

Source: https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui/blob/main/docs/exploding-input/doc.mdx

<DemoPreview className="overflow-visible">
    ```tsx file=./demo.tsx
    ```

## Installation

<InstallationTabs item="exploding-input">
```tsx file=../../registry/spell-ui/exploding-input.tsx
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { ExplodingInput } from "@/components/exploding-input";
```
```tsx
<label className="block">
  <input
    type="text"
    placeholder="try@spell.here"
    className="w-72 p-0 h-10 text-base border-b bg-background font-medium placeholder:font-medium outline-none"
  />
  <ExplodingInput
  className="z-50"
    content={[
      <span key="1" className="text-4xl">🤩</span>,
      <span key="2" className="text-4xl">👾</span>,
      <span key="3" className="text-4xl">😺</span>,
      <span key="4" className="text-4xl">👻</span>,
      <span key="5" className="text-4xl">🎃</span>,
      <span key="6" className="text-4xl">🖤</span>,
      <span key="7" className="text-4xl">🗯️</span>,
    ]}
    direction={{ horizontal: "left", vertical: "top" }}
    gravity={0.5}
    duration={3}
    count={3}
  />
</label>
```

## Props

      name: "content",
      type: "ReactNode[]",
      default: "[]",
      nameDetails: "Array of React nodes to render as particles"
      name: "count",
      type: "number",
      default: "1",
      nameDetails: "Number of particles to spawn per input event (1-5)"
      name: "direction",
      type: "{ horizontal, vertical }",
      default: "{ horizontal: 'center', vertical: 'top' }",
      typeDetails: "horizontal: 'left' | 'center' | 'right', vertical: 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom'"
      name: "gravity",
      type: "number",
      default: "0.7",
      nameDetails: "Gravity value from -1 to 1 (negative = upward)"
      name: "duration",
      type: "number",
      default: "3",
      nameDetails: "Duration of particle animation in seconds"
      name: "scale",
      type: "{ value, randomize, randomVariation }",
      default: "{ value: 1 }",
      typeDetails: "value: base scale, randomize: boolean, randomVariation: percentage (0-100)"
      name: "rotation",
      type: "{ value, animate }",
      default: "{ value: 0 }",
      typeDetails: "value: initial rotation in degrees, animate: enable random rotation animation"
      nameDetails: "CSS classes for the container"
      name: "style",
      type: "CSSProperties",
      nameDetails: "Custom styles for the container"

## Props

# doc.mdx

Source: https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui/blob/main/docs/introduction/doc.mdx

Spell UI is a curated collection of reusable components, blocks, and templates designed to help you build captivating landing pages and user-focused marketing materials with ease.

### Philosophy

Great design is more than just aesthetics. It's a cornerstone of building trust with your audience. In a digital world, your design is often the first impression a visitor has of your brand. It’s the key to answering critical questions in their minds before they commit to engaging with your business, whether that’s signing up, making a purchase, or sharing their data.

Visitors might wonder:

- Is this brand trustworthy?
- Does this feel professional and reliable?
- Will my experience with this product be as polished as its presentation?

Poor design can signal carelessness or lack of attention to detail, leaving users hesitant. Thoughtful, high-quality design communicates confidence, reliability, and care. It suggests that if a team invests in the smallest details of their interface, they likely prioritize excellence in their product and customer experience as well.

A shining example of this philosophy in action is the landing page for Vercel, which has inspired countless users since its debut. Its clean, intentional design instantly conveys quality, making you trust the product before even trying it.

Spell UI draws heavy inspiration from the elegance and simplicity of shadcn/ui, reimagining it with a magical twist to help you craft delightful, trust-building user experiences.

## Community

- [Github Repository](https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui)
- [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/CxzqwQ2EAa)
- [Twitter/X](https://x.com/spell_ui)

---

# doc.mdx

Source: https://github.com/xxtomm/spell-ui/blob/main/docs/mcp/doc.mdx

import { CodeBlockCommand } from '@/components/code-block-command'

## Installation

1. Enable [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro) in your project environment. (Supports Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

<CodeBlockCommand mcp/>

2. Add the registry to your project

Add the following to your components.json file:

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@spell": "https://spell.sh/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

### Usage

You can now ask your IDE to use any Spell UI component. Here are some examples:

- "Add a badge component"
- "Add a blur reveal animation"
- "Add a vertical marquee of logos"

---

    ```

## Installation

<InstallationTabs item="pop-button">
```tsx file=../../registry/spell-ui/pop-button.tsx
```

<details>
<summary>Font Setup (Optional)</summary>

To use the playful DynaPuff font with this component:

1. Add the font to your `layout.tsx`:

```tsx
import { DynaPuff } from 'next/font/google'

const dynaPuff = DynaPuff({
  subsets: ['latin'],
  variable: '--font-dyna-puff',
})

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode
}) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body className={dynaPuff.variable}>
        {children}
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

2. Add the CSS variable to your `globals.css`:

```css
:root {
  --font-pop: var(--font-dyna-puff);
}
```

</details>

<InstallationTabs item="spotify-card">
```tsx file=../../registry/spell-ui/spotify-card.tsx
```

## API Route

This component requires an API route to fetch Spotify metadata. Create the following file:

<code className="bg-muted/50 dark:text-neutral-300 text-neutral-600 p-1.5 rounded-md before:hidden after:hidden">app/api/spotify/route.ts</code>

```ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
// @ts-expect-error no types available
import spotifyUrlInfo from "spotify-url-info";

const { getPreview } = spotifyUrlInfo(fetch) as {
  getPreview: (url: string) => Promise<{
    title: string;
    artist: string;
    image: string;
    link: string;
    audio: string;
  }>;
};

function normalizeSpotifyUrl(url: string): string {
  return url.replace(/\/intl-[a-z]{2}\//, "/");
}

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  const url = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get("url");

  if (!url) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "URL is required" }, { status: 400 });
  }

  try {
    const normalizedUrl = normalizeSpotifyUrl(url);
    const data = await getPreview(normalizedUrl);

    return NextResponse.json({
      title: data.title,
      artist: data.artist,
      image: data.image,
      link: data.link,
      audio: data.audio,
    });
  } catch {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: "Failed to fetch Spotify data" },
      { status: 500 }
    );
  }
}
```

    <SpotifyCardCarouselDemo />

      nameDetails: "Additional CSS classes to apply to the card",
